correctness.rationale: The finite star matrix has a Schur-complement resolvent exactly equal to the normalized Boolean Cauchy transform and centered unit variance. Strict monotonicity of its secular equation yields r+1 simple roots and positive weights. Implicit-function expansions at ±1 give the outer entropy contribution (2s2-3m²)/(4n); expansion at every Nevanlinna zero q_j gives mass c_j/n and log-position -log(n)/2+log|q_j|. Normalization proves sum c_j=v, yielding the stated full coefficient. An exact q_j=0 gives a positive spectral atom at zero and infinite relative entropy. The symmetric three-Nevanlinna-atom family has fixed first four moments yet all-real second coefficient; the monotonic logarithmic formula proves this. The standalone numerical checker independently recomputes finite spectra and passes 116 assertions, including a published special case. Its finite tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The evaluated new claim is a complete finite-Nevanlinna-atom second-order entropy coefficient and an all-real fixed-four-moment coefficient range. Pan 2026 Theorem 1.3 proves only the leading logarithmic term; its Example 4.1 specifies one four-atom spectral formula which does imply the second coefficient for that already-covered special case. The new general formula uses every zero/residue pair of an arbitrary finite Nevanlinna law, and its fixed-four-moment varying-scale family is not implied by the single example. The 2025/early-2026 papers supply definition, monotonicity and inequalities, not this expansion. The supporting numerical/spectral computations cannot establish literature uniqueness; residual old-perturbation-formula risk remains.
residual_risks: The 2026 primary paper contains exact roots in one four-point special case; the exact 1/n coefficient in that special case is already algebraically implied and is not independently novel.
Some equivalent general finite-rank logarithmic-spectral perturbation formula might occur in older matrix/Boolean-probability literature not located by title, abstract or semantic search.
The remaining o(1/n) estimate is pointwise for fixed input law, with no uniformity near colliding atoms, vanishing weights or zero crossing.

value.rationale: The motivating general theorem identifies only v log(n)/(2n); its first omitted 1/n coefficient is a mathematically natural next-order invariant relevant to interpreting quantitative Boolean central-limit rates. The new interlacing spectral-residue formula classifies it for every fixed finite Nevanlinna support and locates the exact infinite-entropy boundary. More substantially, a fixed-four-moment family realizes every real second coefficient. This is a structural obstruction to extending leading-moment universality to the next order, not an arbitrary finite computation or an isolated routine Taylor substitution.
